initial_plan.can_answer: partly: the data can show the annual number of recorded pedestrian injuries and deaths in reported Brooklyn crashes, but not pedestrian exposure or safety risk per trip/person-mile
initial_plan.metric: Annual number of pedestrian casualties, calculated as the sum of number_of_pedestrians_injured and number_of_pedestrians_killed
initial_plan.population: Police-reported motor vehicle crashes in Brooklyn, counted within each calendar year from 2013 through the latest year represented in the file
initial_plan.years: 2013 through the latest year represented in the file; inspect coverage to determine whether the first or last year is partial

facts.borough_before_filter: Of 2,168,642 dated crashes in 2013-2026, 668,406 have borough missing/unknown, 0 have an unrecognized borough, and 483,501 are Brooklyn
facts.missing_crash_date: 0 Brooklyn rows have a missing crash_date year
facts.pedestrian_outcome_missing: 0 Brooklyn rows are missing number_of_pedestrians_injured; 0 are missing number_of_pedestrians_killed; 0 rows have either missing

decisions_and_implications.borough_filter: Keep only records explicitly labeled Brooklyn. The 668,406 missing/unknown-borough crashes cannot be assigned to Brooklyn and are excluded; disclose this limitation. No unrecognized borough values were found.
decisions_and_implications.crash_date_grouping: No Brooklyn rows have a missing crash year; all full calendar years in the final range can be grouped. The analysis excludes the partial 2026 year rather than compare a partial period with full years.
decisions_and_implications.pedestrian_outcome_sums: Keep all Brooklyn rows in complete years; neither pedestrian outcome column is missing in any of the checked Brooklyn rows.

data_check.plan_change: Narrow the final comparison to complete calendar years 2013-2025 because the latest available year, 2026, ends on June 11 and is partial.

final_plan.can_answer: partly: the data show recorded pedestrian casualty counts in police-reported Brooklyn motor vehicle crashes, but do not provide pedestrian exposure or risk per trip/person-mile, so they cannot establish overall pedestrian safety
final_plan.metric: Annual count of reported pedestrian casualties, defined as number_of_pedestrians_injured plus number_of_pedestrians_killed across Brooklyn crashes
final_plan.population: Police-reported motor vehicle crashes explicitly labeled Brooklyn in complete calendar years 2013-2025; the metric counts the reported pedestrian injured and killed fields
filters: retain rows only when both pedestrian outcome fields are present; data check found no missing values
final_plan.years: Complete calendar years 2013-2025; exclude partial 2026 (file coverage ends 2026-06-11)
final_plan.limitations: This is a count of reported pedestrian casualties, not a pedestrian risk rate or a measure adjusted for walking exposure. 668,406 of 2,168,642 dated crashes from 2013-2026 lack a usable borough label and cannot be assigned to Brooklyn; 2026 is partial and excluded.
